conventions.deferred:: A real obligation this plan carries; the suffix names the milestone whose scope in PLAN.md the clause falls in — S6 for the transaction layer. The note names the gap that keeps the clause out of the carrier set. An entry with this value says that nothing under lean/ or vectors/ carries the clause's requirement: a missing carrier is recorded rather than covered by naming a declaration that does not hold the rule. That the milestone's own slice has landed does not make the entry stale — what it records is that the obligation was left uncarried, which is the finding.
conventions.kind: The clause's own keyword, read from the ledger's clause rather than inferred from the coverage class: the class is MUST for both forms, so kind and class diverge for MUST NOT; the three of them in this section are marked MUST NOT here, and the rest MUST.
conventions.uncarried: No declaration and no vector carries the clause's requirement. A declaration that only recognises the vocabulary a clause is written in — reading a field without acting on it, or recording a composite opaquely — is not a carrier; where one of those exists the note names it as the near-miss so a reader can see why it was not counted.
conventions.formalized:: A declaration under `lean/` that carries the clause, by fully qualified name. **A clause may be carried in part, and when it is, the entry names both halves**: the `formalized:` values are what is carried and a `deferred:` value names what is not, with the note saying which half is which — this file's first three entries are of that form, each a sentence covering a transfer and a disposition where only the disposition side has a carrier. The form exists because the alternative is worse in both directions: a bare `formalized:` would claim a half-sentence is finished, and a bare `deferred:` would hide that a declaration already implements part of it, which is what a reader is looking for when they ask what a clause still owes.

design_consequences: **Three of the 18 must-class clauses of txn-work are now carried in part** (`.1` and `.16` in the section, and the acquisition sentence in its doc), each with the half still pending named in its note and the pending half being the *transfer* side of an association the layer never sees; the other fifteen are uncarried, and the reason is structural rather than an omission. The obligations attach to transactional delivery states, so carrying them needs a delivery a transaction can acquire, and neither layer holds one: Spec.Transactions is a machine over txn-ids and says so (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:49-58, :411-419), and Spec.Message records the two transaction delivery states as .unmodelled and moves nothing (lean/Spec/Message.lean:885-890). Each points at the other, and this file records the gap.

Two sentences mandate 'the transaction-error error' for causes no member of that choice names: .4 (a discharge attempted against a transaction a partial delivery was posted to) and .8 (a delivery associated with a different non-discharged transaction than the outcome). The family is named rather than a member, and the cause is one the model cannot reach.
.21 mandates 'the default outcome', which the part names once and defines nowhere; the phrase has no value in the part for a resource to apply.

The ledger keys one sentence twice — .14 and .15 carry the same text and the same digest — so both entries decide the same words, which is what the disposition mechanism requires of a duplicated statement.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: When traveling in the other direction, from resource to controller, the «transfer» and «disposition» frames indicate work performed, and the txn-ids included MUST correctly indicate with which (if any) transaction this work is associated.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: **Carried in part, and the halves are named because a `formalized:` covering half a sentence conflates finished work with pending work.** Carried: resource-to-controller frame whose state is a transactional-state — `SpecAMQP.Spec.Transactions.transactionalState` is the rule and `SpecAMQP.Spec.Transactions.Layer.knows` the predicate it reads, reached from `step`'s transactional-state arm on the disposition side, with the reference's independent reading in `SpecAMQP.Ref.Transactions.onTransactionalState` over `Layer.holds`; the refusal names `unknown-id`, a member of `transaction-error`. Pending: a *transfer*'s txn-id — the sentence covers transfer and disposition, and the layer is handed the disposition's state and the payload only, so a resource-to-controller transfer carrying a bad txn-id is admitted until Session hands the transfer's delivery state over. The report that carried it is `4c7f4f1`, and the handover it waits on is queued as its own slice because it needs the contract's `step` signature changed and `Session` to pass the transfer's delivery state across.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If a transaction is discharged at a point where a message has been transactionally acquired, but has not been fully sent (i.e., the delivery of the message will require more than one «transfer» frame and at least one, but not all, such frames have been sent), then the resource MUST interpret this to mean that the fate of the acquisition is fully decided by the discharge.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the acquisition and its partial sending are not modelled. `Layer` holds txn-ids and nothing about acquisitions (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:197-209), and XXX retires an id without consulting one. The session does hold a delivery across fragmented transfers (lean/Spec/Session.lean:474, :855-866), which is the shape the sentence is about, and nothing ties that delivery to a transaction — the same missing tie as `.1` and `.16`.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the «discharge» indicates the failure of the transaction the resource MUST abort or complete sending the remainder of the message before completing the discharge.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the model has no sending side to abort or to complete. `transferLink` validates a transfer the corpus supplies and `discharge` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313) retires an id; no declaration emits frames, so 'abort or complete sending the remainder of the message before completing the discharge' is a rule with no code to be built in — the gap `connections.5`'s entry records for the close frame.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the resource is unable to process the delivery it MUST NOT allow the successful discharge of the associated transaction.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: 'the resource is unable to process the delivery' is an application-level input the model does not have, and the discharge machine refuses for two other causes only — a settled frame (illegal state) and an id that is not live (`unknown-id`) (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313-324). Near-miss: `Contracts/Transaction.lean`'s `DischargeUnknownIdRefused` states the id rule over the same function, which is a different cause and is dispositioned with `txn-discharge.1`.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: The resource MUST determine the outcome of the delivery before committing the transaction, and this MUST be communicated to the controller before the acceptance of a successful discharge.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the ordering this sentence requires — the outcome determined before the transaction is committed, and communicated before a successful discharge is accepted — has no carrier. `discharge` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313-324) completes on liveness or on the `fail` flag and consults no outcome, and no declaration holds an outcome it could communicate. The ledger keys this sentence twice, at `.14` and `.15`, with one digest: this entry and `.15` decide the same words, as the mechanism requires.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: The resource MUST determine the outcome of the delivery before committing the transaction, and this MUST be communicated to the controller before the acceptance of a successful discharge.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the ordering this sentence requires — the outcome determined before the transaction is committed, and communicated before a successful discharge is accepted — has no carrier. `discharge` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313-324) completes on liveness or on the `fail` flag and consults no outcome, and no declaration holds an outcome it could communicate. The ledger keys this sentence twice, at `.14` and `.15`, with one digest: the `.14` entry beside this one and this entry decide the same words, as the mechanism requires.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: The outcome communicated by the resource MUST be associated with the same transaction with which the «transfer» from controller to resource was associated.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: **Carried in part, and the halves are named because a `formalized:` covering half a sentence conflates finished work with pending work.** Carried: an outcome the resource communicates being associated with a transaction this endpoint holds, checked against the register — `SpecAMQP.Spec.Transactions.transactionalState` is the rule and `SpecAMQP.Spec.Transactions.Layer.knows` the predicate it reads, reached from `step`'s transactional-state arm on the disposition side, with the reference's independent reading in `SpecAMQP.Ref.Transactions.onTransactionalState` over `Layer.holds`; the refusal names `unknown-id`, a member of `transaction-error`. Pending: 'the same transaction with which the transfer from controller to resource was associated' — nothing carries a transfer-side txn-id for the outcome's id to be compared with, so *sameness* is unstateable. The report that carried it is `4c7f4f1`, and the handover it waits on is queued as its own slice because it needs the contract's `step` signature changed and `Session` to pass the transfer's delivery state across.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the resource can no longer apply the outcome that it originally indicated would be the result of a successful discharge then it MUST NOT allow the successful discharge of the associated transaction.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the model records no outcome that it indicated would follow a successful discharge, so it can never find that the outcome no longer applies. `Layer` holds the transactions, the next id and both ends' capability lists (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:197-209); a discharge's `fail` flag is a boolean the machine reads (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313), not an outcome it stores and later checks.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: After a successful discharge, the state of unsettled deliveries at the resource MUST reflect the outcome that was applied.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the resource holds no unsettled deliveries to reflect an outcome on. `Layer.retire` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:230-231) marks a transaction discharged and moves nothing else, and `Contracts/Settlement.lean`'s closing section records that the sender's unsettled map is not modelled — the session holds one delivery (lean/Spec/Session.lean:474). Near-miss: `Spec.Message.recordState` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:1013) applies an outcome to a delivery when the corpus asks it to, not when a discharge succeeds.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the transaction controller wishes to associate an outgoing «transfer» with a transaction, it MUST set the state of the transfer with a «transactional-state» carrying the appropriate transaction identifier.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: nothing obliges a sender to state an outgoing transfer's transaction as a `transactional-state`, and the transfer's `state` field is read nowhere. `transferLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:815-921) reads delivery-id, delivery-tag, message-format, settled, aborted and more, and never the delivery state, so an outgoing transfer that carries transactional work may carry it in any spelling or none. `deliveryStateOfValue` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:940) can read such a state, which is a reader for a frame the corpus supplies rather than a requirement on a sender.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: At this point the controller can no longer influence the state of the delivery as it is settled, and the resource MUST apply the default outcome.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the sentence joins two obligations and neither has a carrier. Nothing freezes a delivery's state when it is settled: `Spec.Message.recordState` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:1013) accumulates the settled flag and a later state is still applied to a delivery that is settled but not terminal, and `applyState`'s refusal (lean/Spec/Message.lean:1031) is about a terminal state rather than a settled one. And 'the default outcome' is named once in the whole part and defined nowhere, so the resource's obligation has no value to apply.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: Note that if delivery is split across several «transfer» frames then all frames MUST be explicitly associated with the same transaction.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the same association as `.2`, one frame at a time. The fragmentation state this sentence needs exists — `Session.delivery` is held across a delivery's transfers (lean/Spec/Session.lean:474) — and `transferLink` compares the three identity fields a continuation may contradict (lean/Spec/Session.lean:862-876) while the delivery state, and with it the transaction, is compared nowhere. A continuation that changes or omits the transaction its earlier frames named is admitted.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If this happens, the control link MUST be terminated with the «transaction-rollback» error.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: 'this' is a discharge attempted against a transaction a partial delivery has been posted to, and the model has neither the partial delivery nor a state to raise the refusal from. `discharge` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313-324) retires an id on liveness alone, and `Spec.Transactions`' own docstring names this sentence as the one needing fragmentation state the layer does not have (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:49-58). **The mandated condition is a member, and this note said otherwise until it was read against the clause**: the sentence names «transaction-rollback», so nothing is missing from the declared surface — which its own recitation of the members showed, since `transaction-rollback` is one of them. What is missing is the **state that detects the violation**: the model holds no partial delivery and no delivery-to-transaction association, so there is nothing for a discharge to be attempted against.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: On receiving a non-settled delivery associated with a live transaction, the transactional resource MUST inform the controller of the presumptive terminal outcome before it can successfully discharge the transaction.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the ordering the sentence states — the presumptive terminal outcome informed before the discharge can succeed — is enforced nowhere. `discharge` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313) never asks whether an outcome was communicated, and `dispositionLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:985-1019) requires no prior disposition, because the session holds a delivery that belongs to a link and not to a transaction. Near-miss: `Spec.Message.applyState` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:1031) is how a state is applied to a delivery at a node — the vocabulary this sentence is written in, not the obligation it states.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: That is, the resource MUST send a «disposition» performative which covers the posted transfer with the state of the delivery being a «transactional-state» with the correct transaction identified, and a terminal outcome.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the performative `.5` obliges the resource to send, and no declaration requires a sender to send one. The reading half is present — `Spec.Message.deliveryStateOfValue` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:940) recognises a `transactional-state` as a state a disposition may carry, and `Spec.Session.stepTransactionState` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:1072) routes a disposition's state to the transaction layer — but the model never builds a frame from an obligation; the corpus supplies every frame, which is the same gap `connections.5`'s entry beside `deferred:S4` records for the close frame.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: However, the delivery MUST NOT be associated with a different non-discharged transaction than the outcome.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: a MUST NOT over an association the model does not make. Neither the held transaction nor the held delivery carries the other's id — `Layer` holds transactions, the next id and capability lists (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:197-209) and `Session` holds one delivery (lean/Spec/Session.lean:474) — so the prohibited pair cannot be formed and no comparison could detect it. The model's only liveness question is `Layer.live` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:216-217), which asks whether an id is still in use rather than which delivery an outcome belongs to.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If this happens then the control link MUST be terminated with a «transaction-rollback» error.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried: the termination `.7`'s violation would mandate. The violation cannot be detected (see `.7`), and the control link's only mandated termination is the rollback of the transactions it created — `Layer.retireAll` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:237-238), reached through `Session.afterLinkRelease` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:599) — which retires ids rather than refusing the frame that broke the rule. The condition is named as the `transaction-error` family, and no member of it names this cause.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the link endpoint does not support transactional acquisition, the link MUST be terminated with a «not-implemented» error.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: deferred: S6 — uncarried, and unenforced by design: the model has no source for the missing input. Whether a link endpoint supports transactional acquisition would be read from the flow frame's `properties` map, and no declaration reads a flow's properties — `flowLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:742-806) reads the link's own fields and the handle it must name. `Contracts/Transaction.lean:43-44` records this clause's `amqp-error` as stated in the ledger as unenforced rather than approximated, which is what this entry does.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: An outcome sent by the controller before the transaction has discharged MUST be associated with the same transaction.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: **Carried in part, and the halves are named because a `formalized:` covering half a sentence conflates finished work with pending work.** Carried: an outcome naming an id the register does not hold being refused, in either direction — `SpecAMQP.Spec.Transactions.transactionalState` is the rule and `SpecAMQP.Spec.Transactions.Layer.knows` the predicate it reads, reached from `step`'s transactional-state arm on the disposition side, with the reference's independent reading in `SpecAMQP.Ref.Transactions.onTransactionalState` over `Layer.holds`; the refusal names `unknown-id`, a member of `transaction-error`. Pending: sameness with the transaction the acquisition was posted under, which needs the acquisition the delivery-state layer would hold. The report that carried it is `4c7f4f1`, and the handover it waits on is queued as its own slice because it needs the contract's `step` signature changed and `Session` to pass the transfer's delivery state across.
